questions.q_en:

The manager postponed the meeting because several important documents were still missing.

Identify whether the highlighted group of words is a phrase or a clause.

questions.solution_en:
Answer: C) Clause

Explanation: A clause is a group of words that contain both a subject and a verb. A phrase does not contain a complete subject-verb combination.

In the highlighted part:

“several important documents” = subject, “were” = verb

Since the group contains both a subject and a verb, it is a clause.

The highlighted phrase:

“with exceptional communication skills” describes the noun “employees.”

Which employees? → employees with exceptional communication skills

Therefore, it functions as an adjective phrase.

Explanation: A participial phrase begins with a participle and functions as an adjective.

The highlighted phrase begins with:

“Having completed” which is a participle form.

The phrase describes the “senior analyst.”

Which analyst? → analyst having completed the presentation successfully

Therefore, it is a participial phrase.

Why other options are incorrect:

A) An infinitive phrase begins with “to + verb.”

B) A gerund phrase functions as a noun.

D) A noun phrase functions as a noun and does not begin with a participle.

questions.q_en:
Identify the grammatical function of the highlighted non-finite phrase.

The students gathered in the auditorium to attend the orientation program conducted by the university administration.
questions.q_hi:
Identify the grammatical function of the highlighted non-finite phrase.

The students gathered in the auditorium to attend the orientation program conducted by the university administration.
questions.solution_en:
Answer: C) Functioning as an adverb

Explanation: An infinitive phrase can function as a noun, adjective, or adverb.

The highlighted phrase:

“to attend the orientation program conducted by the university administration” modifies the verb “gathered” and tells the purpose of gathering.

gathered why? → to attend the orientation program

Therefore, the phrase functions as an adverb.

Why other options are incorrect:

A) A noun functions as subject/object/complement.

B) An adjective modifies a noun/pronoun, but this phrase modifies the verb “gathered.”

D) The subject of the sentence is “The students.”

questions.q_en:
Identify the type of the highlighted non-finite phrase.

The officer noticed a group of volunteers distributing food and medical supplies to the flood victims.
questions.q_hi:
Identify the type of the highlighted non-finite phrase.

The officer noticed a group of volunteers distributing food and medical supplies to the flood victims.
questions.solution_en:
Answer: B) Participial Phrase

Explanation: A participial phrase begins with a participle and functions as an adjective.

The highlighted phrase begins with:

“distributing” which is a present participle.

The phrase describes “volunteers.”

Which volunteers? → volunteers distributing food and medical supplies

Therefore, it is a participial phrase.

Why other options are incorrect:

A) A gerund phrase functions as a noun, but this phrase describes a noun.

C) An infinitive phrase begins with “to + verb.”

D) A prepositional phrase begins with a preposition such as in, on, at, with, etc.
